subject: Civic Education
lesson: Explains the duties and responsibilities of public service institutions: 1-Minute Frozen Tableau Drama: Competency Level 8.1.3
unique_learning_outcome: Explains the duties and responsibilities of public service institutions.
Explains the importance of providing efficent service of the officers of public services identifying the need.
the_entrance: 5-minute introduction: Teacher introduces the topic 'Duties and Responsibilities of Public Service Institutions' and connects it to the students' prior knowledge and everyday experience. The teacher explains that public service institutions, such as schools, hospitals, and police stations, play a crucial role in providing essential services to the community. The teacher then asks students to imagine they are part of a public service institution and to think about the duties and responsibilities that come with it. This leads directly into the selected activity.

summary: Students will understand the duties and responsibilities of public service institutions and the importance of providing efficient service.

post_activity: 5-minute in-class assignment: Students will write a short reflection on what they learned about the duties and responsibilities of public service institutions and how they can apply it in their daily lives.
selected_activity:
Activity: 1-Minute Frozen Tableau Drama: Competency Level 8.1.3
Approach: Students use 1-minute frozen tableau drama to explore 'Explains the duties and responsibilities of public service institutions.'. Students take civic roles, respond to a shared scenario, and agree on a reasoned decision. Standard class layout (35 students): Desks arranged into 7 teams (7 teams (7 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Student task: Students take civic roles, respond to a shared scenario, and agree on a reasoned decision. Standard class layout (35 students): Desks arranged into 7 teams (7 teams (7 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Teacher facilitation: Organizes all 35 students using 7 teams (7 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer. and monitors progress with outcome-focused prompts and time checks. Circulates across 7 teams, facilitating role execution and formatively checking progress.
Expected output: A short role-based civic decision and its reasons.
Grouping: 7 teams (7 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer.
